raw_recipe.headline: Smoked Salmon Spread
raw_recipe.description: This salmon spread recipe with smoked salmon, cream cheese, dill, scallions, and hot sauce is easy to make and always gets so many compliments!
raw_recipe.name: Smoked Salmon Spread

recipeInstructions.text: Stir cream cheese in a bowl until no longer in block form. Add salmon, green onion, dill, Worcestershire sauce, and hot pepper sauce; mix until well combined.

review.reviewBody: I just made this for a party and several people really raved about it and wanted the recipe. Easy to make, too! I doubled the worcestershire and hot pepper sauce. Also, I didn't have fresh dill or green onion, so I used dried dill and dehydrated onion flakes. Thanks for this recipe!

This recipe is great as is but I combined it with another and loved the results. I thinned out the cream cheese with 1/2 cup heavy cream, added 2 tsp. lemon juice, 1 clove minced garlic, a little horseradish sauce (to taste), 1 Tbls. drained capers and more dill. I piped it onto cocktail rye bread and sliced cucumber rounds and garnished them with sprigs of fresh dill. They were devoured instantly and guests were begging for the recipe. One guest mother even called me the next day for the recipe because he told her how good it was. Thank you for sharing this delight!

good guideline recipe, you need to go by taste. I used 3 cans of salmon, adding 1/4tsp of liquid smoke per can. Then 2 pkgs of cream cheese. I doubled or more the dill, added about 2-3Tbsp. of lemon juice (gives a great depth to the flavor), and used dried onion since I didn't have any green onion (about half of what it called for, maybe a bit more). I used the food processor to process all but one can of salmon, and added it at the end and just pulsated it to give a chunky texture. I served with ritz, triscuits, and wheat thins, but I think the Ritz were the best. Will make this again, so good I licked the food processor bowl out! ;D

My husband smoked some salmon the other day in hopes that I'd find a good dip recipe. This is it! He can't stop eating it. My caveat to folks is to be sure to use *smoked* salmon (DIY and save a lot of money). I added a little more salmon than the recipe called for, and I didn't have fresh dill, so I used dried dill (1/2 the amount called for). Finally, I mixed everything in a food processor to get a nice consistency.

I had a 14-oz. prepared smoked salmon packet and I used all of it, so I added 2 more dashes each of Worcestershire and hot sauces to commensurate. I also blended in about 1 Tbsp of capers, chopped finely. Served the chilled and molded spread with a selection of water crackers at a New Year's Eve party, where compliments flowed about its well-blended flavors.

This recipe is great but with the following improvements (I have made it like this about 10 times now and turns great every time): 1 pack 8oz cream cheese softened at room temp, 7 oz canned Alaskan salmon (red can brand), 3 dashes hot pepper sauce, 1 TB fresh dill, 3 dashes Worcestershire sauce, 2 green onions chopped finely, 1/2 tsp liquid smoke, hot chilli pepper flakes as desired for spiciness. Mix all with a wooden spoon, transfer to a serving dish and place in fridge for 30 min to allow flavors to blend. Delicious!!!

I did as some suggested and doubled the Worcestershire sauce and hot sauce. I also substituted onion powder and freeze-dried chives in place of green onions for two reasons. One, I was honestly too lazy to chop the green onions. Two, I didn't want to bite into green onions. I also whipped the salmon instead of leaving chunks. It was so smooth and fluffy. My whole family loved this recipe!

This was a good base to start with. it needed a lot more flavor to bring out that smoky taste. I knew it wasn't going to be enough green onions, dill, Worcestershire and hot sauce which I used Tabasco. I added more. about ; 2 tablespoons Worcestershire, 1 tablespoon Tabasco, 4 green onions chopped small, 1 tablespoon fresh baby dill chopped fine and added fresh lemon zest from a medium size lemon. added sea salt to enhance the flavor. I kept the same amount of salmon. I will make it again but try smoke dry lox.

Delish! I used half of the cream cheese and salmon, but kept everything else the same. Put everything but the salmon in the food processor, blended it, then added the chopped salmon and just blended until it was all mixed together.

This recipe was awesome. I made a couple of changes. I used fresh smokes trout that I brined in salt and garlic powder than smoked with hickory, Light smoke. I also added 1 tbsp. of old bay seasoning and one cup of chopped pecans. Yuuuuuuuuuuum. Lee

I don't eat salmon (or fish in general) so relied heavily on the reviews of others, and they were right, this recipe is a keeper. The wedding guests I prepared this for loved this recipe, and I as asked for the recipe several times. I reduced the cream cheese and the salmon by half, stuffed in baked wonton cones, with a bit of dill, and these went over like a storm. So good!!! Thank you!

Excellent. I cut it down to meet the portion of leftover smoked salmon and did not use/have the dill. I sub'd shallot for the green onion. I recall a similar recipe that called for capers and that little touch of sour contributed well...just a thought. This is simple and fast to make. I am looking forward to tomorrow as I expect it will be even better. Thanks, wahine.
Easy and quick way to make an enjoyable smoked salmon I just brought back from Seattle. Like one review, I also added capers.
How about adding a bit of horseradish??

This is so quick and easy, and super yummy! Great simple solution for entertaining. I might like to add some garlic next time. I could also see capers being a good addition as another reviewer suggested.
Made it exactly as recipe says. We loved it! Served it on toasted French baguettes.
Easy. Love it on a bagel! Used capers instead of dill.

It was delicious, well definitely make it again. I left out the hot pepper sauce only because my stomach will not tolerate it. I did not miss it at all. This would be great for a party appetizer. I cut the recipe in half and still plenty to eat.

This was very flavorful and easy to make. Luckily I had all the ingredients so it was easy and quick to whip up. Next time I would add more salmon as it was a little creamier than I expected it to be and while there were hints of salmon flavor there wasn’t as much salmon as I would’ve liked. I will definitely be making again though. Thank you for the recipe!
Loved it and was so easy and tasty!
